For the given parallelogram $ABCD$, the CORRECT option is
I. $\angle B = \angle C$
II. $AB = CD$
III. $\angle D = 180^\circ - t^\circ$
explanation: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal ($AB = CD$, II), and consecutive angles are supplementary ($\angle D + \angle C = 180^\circ \implies \angle D = 180^\circ - t^\circ$, III). Adjacent angles are generally not equal, so I is false.

The given figure shows a triangle $ABC$, where $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of sides $AC$ and $AB$ respectively. The CORRECT option will be
I. $AD = AE$
II. $DE = \frac{1}{2} BC$
III. $DE$ is parallel to $BC$
explanation: By the Midpoint Theorem, the line segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side ($DE \parallel BC$, III) and equal to half its length ($DE = \frac{1}{2}BC$, II).
